Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 32, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Sajda (The Prostration), because it contains the verse of prostration and the description of the believers who prostrate to Allah, the Exalted, upon hearing the verses of the Mighty Qur'an.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Mention of the signs of (Allah's) power and His oneness, and drawing attention to the existence of the One, the Subduer, through the traces of His power in the upper and lower created beings and what lies between them, and the arrangement of this universe. Speaking of the specific creation of man with this wondrous formation and exquisite shaping, all of this within the context of refuting the divinity of anyone other than Allah, the Exalted.

• Refutation of the creed of the polytheists, to which the weakness of their minds led them: denying the Resurrection and considering it far-fetched that they would be brought to life a second time, because their bodies decay and vanish into the earth. He answers them with the logic of sound reason: that re-creation is easier than initial creation, though everything is easy and simple for Allah.

• Depiction of the state of humiliation and disgrace that the criminals will face in the place of gathering, and the wishes they will make to return to the world and correct their deeds; and speaking of the people of happiness in contrast to them, praising those who believe in the verses of Allah, and mentioning the bliss that Allah has prepared for them.

• Speaking of the Day of Reckoning, on which Allah, the Exalted, will judge between the creatures with His justice; and an indication of the destruction of the wrongdoing deniers, and a warning to them of the victory that will be granted to the believers; and the command to the Messenger ﷺ to turn away from them.

[Tafsir]

﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been given at the beginning of Surat al-Baqara.
This Qur'an that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought is, without doubt, sent down from Allah, the Lord of all creation.

Or do they say, "He has invented it"? No, it is the truth, established, sent down to you, O Messenger, from your Lord, so that you may warn with it a people to whom no warner came before you, so that they may be guided: that they may know the truth, believe in it, prefer it, and believe in you. (ﷺ)

Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, for a wisdom known to Him. He is able to create them with the word "Kun" (Be), and so they come to be. Then He rose over His Throne, glorified and exalted is He, that is, He rose and ascended above it, in a manner befitting His majesty, without asking how (la yukayyaf), and without likening it to the rising of created beings (la yushabbah). You have no protector (wali) besides Him to manage your affairs, nor any intercessor (shafi') who will intercede for you with Allah, so that you may be saved from His punishment. Will you not then take heed and reflect, O people, so that you single out Allah for divinity (al-uluhiyyah) and devote worship sincerely to Him?

God directs the affairs of creation from the heaven to the earth, then that command and arrangement ascends back up to Him in a day whose measure is a thousand years of the days of this world that you count.

That is the Creator who manages the affairs of all the worlds. He knows everything that is hidden from sight, what the breasts conceal and the souls keep secret, and He knows what has been witnessed by sight. He is the Mighty, the Victorious who cannot be overcome, the Merciful to His believing servants.
Allah is the One who perfected the creation of everything, and began the creation of man, who is Adam (peace be upon him), from clay.
Then He made the offspring of Adam to descend from a weak, fragile, and humble fluid (nutfah).

Then He completed the creation of man and perfected it, and made his form good, and breathed into him of His spirit by sending the angel to him, so that he would breathe the spirit into him. And He made for you, O people, the blessing of hearing and sight, by which you distinguish between sounds, colors, essences and persons, and the blessing of intellect, by which you distinguish between good and evil, and between the beneficial and the harmful. Little are you thankful to your Lord for what He has bestowed upon you.

The polytheists, who associate partners with God and deny the Resurrection, said: "When our flesh and bones have turned to dust in the earth, shall we really be raised up in a new creation?" They find this far-fetched, not seeking to reach the truth; rather, this comes from them out of wrongdoing and obstinacy, for they disbelieve in meeting their Lord on the Day of Resurrection.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: The Angel of Death, who has been entrusted with you, will take your souls [i.e., cause you to die] when your terms have ended, and you will not be delayed for a single moment. Then you will be returned to your Lord, and He will recompense you for all your deeds: if [they are] good, then good, and if [they are] evil, then evil.

Had you seen, O listener, when the criminals who denied the Resurrection will hang their heads before their Lord out of disgrace and shame, saying: "Our Lord, we have seen our ugly deeds and heard from You the confirmation of what Your messengers used to command us in the world, and we have now repented to You. So return us to the world that we may act in it by Your obedience. Indeed, we now have certain knowledge of what we used to deny in the world concerning Your oneness, and that You will resurrect those in the graves." Had you seen all of that, O listener, you would have seen a tremendous matter and a grave calamity.

If We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance, but My word has come into effect and is binding: I will surely fill Hell with disbelievers and sinners from among both the jinn and mankind, all of them. That is because they chose misguidance over guidance.

It is said to these polytheists, as they enter the Fire, by way of rebuke: "Taste the punishment, because of your heedlessness of the Hereafter and your immersion in the pleasures of this world. Indeed, We have left you today in the punishment. And taste the punishment of Hell, which never ends, for what you used to do in the world of disbelief in Allah and disobedience to Him."

Only those truly believe in the verses of the Qur'an and act upon them, those who, when they are admonished by them or when they are recited to them, fall down in prostration to their Lord, humbly submissive and obedient. They glorify God in their prostration, praising Him, and they are not too proud to prostrate and to glorify Him, and to worship Him alone, with no partner.

Their sides rise up from their beds: those who believe in the signs of God, they pray to their Lord in the night prayer, calling upon their Lord out of fear of punishment and desire for reward, and from what We have provided them they spend in obedience to God and in His cause.
No soul knows what is kept hidden for these believers of delight to the eye and comfort to the heart, as a reward for their righteous deeds.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 32, verse 18:**

Is one who was obedient to Allah and His Messenger, believing in His promise and His warning, like one who disbelieved in Allah and His messengers and denied the Last Day? They are not equal in the sight of Allah.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 32, verse 19:

As for those who believed in God and acted upon what they were commanded, their reward is gardens in which they will take shelter, and they will dwell in their bliss as a hospitality for them, a recompense for what they used to do in the world by obeying Him.

As for those who departed from obedience to Allah and committed His acts of disobedience, their abode is Hellfire. Whenever they wish to leave it, they will be returned into it. And it will be said to them, as rebuke and reproach: "Taste the punishment of the Fire, which you used to deny in the worldly life."

And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment, the trials, afflictions and calamities of this world, before the greater punishment on the Day of Resurrection, when they will be tormented in the Fire of Hell; so that perhaps they will return and repent of their sins.

And who is more unjust than one who has been reminded of the signs of his Lord, then turned away from them all, neglecting their admonitions, but rather was arrogant towards them? Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals who turned away from the signs and proofs of Allah and did not benefit from them.

And We certainly gave Moses the Torah, just as We have given you, O Messenger, the Qur'an. So do not be in doubt about meeting Moses on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj. And We made the Torah a guidance for the Children of Israel, calling them to the truth and to a straight path.

We made from among the Children of Israel leaders who guided others and called to goodness, whom people followed, calling them to monotheism, the worship of God alone, and obedience to Him. They attained this high rank only when they were patient in carrying out God's commands, in abstaining from what He forbade, in calling to Him, and in bearing harm in His cause; and they affirmed the signs and proofs of God with certain conviction.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 32, verse 25:

Indeed your Lord, O Messenger, will judge between the believers and the disbelievers, among the Children of Israel and others, on the Day of Resurrection, with justice, concerning what they differed about in matters of religion, and He will recompense every person according to his deeds, by admitting the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of the Fire into the Fire.

Do these disbelievers in the Messenger not see how many generations before them We destroyed, through whose dwellings they walk, witnessing them with their own eyes, like the people of Hud, Salih and Lut? Indeed, in that are signs and admonitions by which the truth of the messengers who came to them is proven, and the falsehood of the polytheism they hold to is shown. Will these deniers of the messengers not listen to God's admonitions and proofs, so that they benefit from them?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 32, verse 27:

Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land, the dry and hard earth in which there is no vegetation, and bring forth thereby crops of varying colors, of which their cattle eat and by which their own bodies are nourished, so that they live by it? Do they not see these blessings with their own eyes, so that they would know that God, who did that, is able to revive the dead and raise them from their graves?

These disbelievers who associate partners with God are asking for the punishment to come quickly, so they say: "When will this judgment come, which will decide between us and you by punishing us, as you claim, if you are truthful in your assertion?"

Say (to them, O Messenger): On the Day of Decision, when your punishment takes place and you witness death, faith will not benefit the disbelievers, nor will they be granted respite for repentance and reconsideration.

Turn away, O Messenger, from these polytheists, pay no heed to their denial, and wait for what Allah will do with them. Indeed, they are waiting and watching for misfortunes to befall you. So Allah will disgrace them and humiliate them, and will grant you victory over them. And He has done so; to Him belong all praise and grace.
